ai.title: Type definitions and terms constants for codebase commercial sales
ai.summary: A new file `common/src/constants/freebuff-codebase-sales.ts` introduces shared type interfaces for a commercial codebase contribution flow, including `CodebaseSalesOffer` which requires a fixed branch map hash and finalized terms text. The module defines a guard function `isCodebaseSalesOffer` that strictly validates field types and regular expressions for repository identifiers, 40-character commit SHAs, and 64-character hash digests. It also exports `CODEBASE_CONTRIBUTION_TERMS_VERSION` and a multi-paragraph license document establishing a nonexclusive license for commercial AI training, with a manually settled one-time reward of 1 to 10,000 Freebucks on the first completed paid license.
ai.evidence: The diff adds a new file `common/src/constants/freebuff-codebase-sales.ts` that defines types (`CodebaseSalesOffer`, `CodebaseSalesSubmission`, `CodebaseSalesProject`) and the `isCodebaseSalesOffer` validation function, and exports constants `CODEBASE_CONTRIBUTION_TERMS_VERSION`, `CODEBASE_CONTRIBUTION_TERMS_URL`, and `CODEBASE_CONTRIBUTION_TERMS_PARAGRAPHS`.
ai.unknowns: The diff provides no evidence of a UI surface, server-side endpoint, or consumer code that reads these new types or constants to display the offer to end users.

eli5.text: A new rulebook and checklist have been added to the core system for a paid program where you contribute your code to a partner. This internal setup defines exactly how offers look, the precise snapshot of code accepted, and a one-time reward of between 1 and 10,000 Freebucks if your contribution is sold. The program is kept separate from your everyday coding experience, and since no user-facing screens or server endpoints read these new types yet, the setup does nothing visible in daily use.

ai.title: Context budget diagnostics and truncated state rewind fixes
ai.summary: The agent runtime now enforces a "receipt floor" on its internal `contextTokenCount` so that the provider's reported prompt size is respected even when history was modified mid-step, preventing Desktop threads from sending prompts up to 990k tokens while the internal counter stayed under the compaction threshold. This is exposed to SDK consumers via a new `onContextOverBudget` callback that reports the discrepancy between the provider's count and the runtime's belief at the moment of the request. Additionally, `truncateRunStateAtUserTurn` in the SDK now accepts `editedText` and `previousText` parameters to correct the rewind cut point when a host transcript includes rows that were refused before the harness ran (such as due to spend limits), which previously caused the state to delete turns the user kept. These changes affect 5 files across the common types, agent runtime, and SDK surfaces.
ai.evidence: The diff adds the `ContextOverBudgetData` type to `common/src/types/contracts/llm.ts` and implements a `receiptFloor` mechanism in `packages/agent-runtime/src/run-agent-step.ts` that floors `contextTokenCount` using the provider's reported token count; it also extends `sdk/src/compact-run-state.ts` to handle rows that never reached the state via `editedText` and `previousText` checks.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show which specific Desktop or CLI surfaces have already wired the `onContextOverBudget` callback to their telemetry or UI.

changes.what: Implement a receipt floor in `loopAgentSteps` to ensure `contextTokenCount` is never below the provider's reported prompt tokens plus output tokens, unless history was explicitly replaced.
Define the `ContextOverBudgetData` contract type to capture the provider's usage, the runtime's decision state, and baseline information for over-budget diagnostics.
Expose the `onContextOverBudget` hook in `RunOptions` and wire it through to the agent runtime's diagnostic logger.
Extend `truncateRunStateAtUserTurn` with logic to detect and skip rows that never reached the persisted state by comparing `editedText` and `previousText` against the prompt content at the cut point.
Add the `DESKTOP_CONTEXT_OVER_BUDGET` analytics event to the enum for tracking instances where provider-reported prompts exceed the agent's context budget.

eli5.text: The AI coding assistant now keeps a more accurate count of how much of its memory is in use, preventing it from silently sending massive requests that exceed its limits. This fix also corrects a rewind error where editing a past message could accidentally delete parts of the conversation that you kept. These are internal stability improvements that ensure your chat history remains intact and the assistant operates within its proper memory boundaries; no user-facing settings or features change.

ai.title: Remove context budget diagnostics and over-budget receipt tracking
ai.summary: The diagnostic subsystem tracking provider-reported context over-budget states has been removed from the agent runtime and shared types. `ContextOverBudgetData` and the `DESKTOP_CONTEXT_OVER_BUDGET` analytics event are no longer defined, and `runAgentStep` no longer returns a `contextReceipt` or enforces a `receiptFloor` on `contextTokenCount`. The removal of the `editedText` and `previousText` parameters from `truncateRunStateAtUserTurn` simplifies the history rewind logic in the SDK.
ai.evidence: The diff removes `DESKTOP_CONTEXT_OVER_BUDGET` from `common/src/constants/analytics-events.ts` and `ContextOverBudgetData` from `common/src/types/contracts/llm.ts`. In `packages/agent-runtime/src/run-agent-step.ts`, the local `StepContextReceipt` type and the `receiptFloor` enforcement logic (which clamped `contextTokenCount` to the provider's reported usage) are deleted, alongside the `onContextOverBudget` callback. The SDK's `truncateRunStateAtUserTurn` in `sdk/src/compact-run-state.ts` drops the `editedText`/`previousText` parameters and the logic that adjusted the rewind boundary based on text mismatches.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not explain why the diagnostic was removed, though it follows a commit that introduced the 'receipt floor' mechanism it now deletes. A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

changes.what: Removed the `DESKTOP_CONTEXT_OVER_BUDGET` analytics event and the `ContextOverBudgetData` contract type.
Deleted the `receiptFloor` logic that clamped context token counts and the `StepContextReceipt` tracking in the agent loop.
Removed the `editedText` and `previousText` parameters and their corresponding boundary-adjustment logic from `truncateRunStateAtUserTurn`.
Removed the `onContextOverBudget` option from `RunOptions` and its forwarding to the agent runtime.

eli5.text: The internal diagnostic tool that tracked when the AI assistant's memory of a conversation got too large has been removed. This is a maintenance update that removes one of the ways the system watched for memory overload; the other safety checks that keep conversations within their limits remain in place. You will see no change in how the assistant behaves, and no action is needed.

ai.title: Mapped contribution offer types for recovered project snapshots
ai.summary: Introduces shared type definitions in `common/src/constants/freebuff-mapped-contributions.ts` for a mapped contribution subsystem. These types model offers for recovered projects bound to immutable prepared snapshots, including fields for terms versioning, package hashing, and offer status transitions. A parallel module `common/src/constants/freebuff-codebase-sales.ts` contains type guards that validate similar snapshot-bound offer structures with commit and reference hashes. The new types support state pagination via `nextCursor` and define request/response unions for accepting, dismissing, or withdrawing offers.
ai.evidence: New file `common/src/constants/freebuff-mapped-contributions.ts` introduces type definitions for `MappedContributionOffer`, `MappedContributionState`, `MappedContributionRequest`, and `MappedContributionResponse` within the `common/` package.
ai.unknowns: The runtime consumer that implements the mapped contribution workflow is not visible in this diff.

eli5.text: The engineering team added the formal rules that define how offers for recovered project snapshots are structured, tracked, and acted upon. This is an internal foundation layer that sets up the data shapes needed for these offers, including their status and associated terms. It does not change how the application works for you today, nor does it make any new features visible or available. The system now has the definitions required to support these offer workflows in the future.
